To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the meta-analyses showed that the risk of CHD and CHD death was significantly lower in the mixed n-3 and 6 PUFA diets than in the n-6 specific diets.
the meta-analysis of the effects of dietary intervention with n-6 PUFAs, which replaced SFA and TFA, showed a 13% increased risk of nonfatal MI+CHD mortality (RR = 1.13; 95%CI: 0.84,1.53).

(i) RCT that increased n-6 fatty acids with specificity (i.e. without also increasing n-3 fatty acids) had no effect on CHD risk, and may have increased the risk of CHD and all-cause death, and (ii) RCT that simultaneously increased n-6 and/or n-3 fatty acid intakes had a significant reduction in risk of CHD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dietary interventions that increase n-6 and/or n-3 PU FA intakes.
dietary interventions that have been used to inform the public on the optimal intake of PUFA.
the effects of specific dietary interventions on CHD risk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
‘the consumption of n-3 PU FA is associated with reduced risk of CHD and all-cause mortality’.

increasing n-6 PUFAs, without increasing n-3 PUFAs, increases the risks of CHDs and death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the advice to consume ‘at least 10 % of energy from PUFA’ is not supported by the available evidence.
the current evidence base is not strong enough to recommend a high n-6 PU fatty acid intake.
the evidence for increasing n-6 PUFAs to reduce the risk of CHD is not compelling and may be misleading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current dietary advice to increase n-6 fatty acid intake, based on the meta-analysis of the mixed n-3 and 6 fatty acid RCT, is likely to be harmful.

n-6 PUFAs should not be singled out and specifically recommended, but rather that n-3 PUFAs should be consumed in combination with n-6 PUFs, as part of a healthy balanced diet, to maximise the benefits of both.
n-6 PUFAs should be replaced with n-3 PUFAs, and not other fats, and that n-3 PUFs should be the main source of dietary PUFA.
